contexts.text: I have slain a man to ray wound () = that he had extinguished faith... A wound... = no more soundness... A wound, in special, = that faith is desolated. AC 431. Illustrated.
An influx (caused them) to wound themselves.
Wound for wound () = if anything of the affection of love that is exteriorly in the will [is injured].
A wound, in the Word, is predicated of the injuring of good; a plague, of the injuring of truth. Illustrated.
The stroke of their wound () = the derivative evil of life. Compare AE 962:5.
Unless (evil) appears, it is like a wound, which is not healed unless it is opened. SE 6031.
He who was wounded by thieves () = those who, through evils and falsities, had been spiritually wounded by the Jews.
Sores, and wounds = evils in the outermosts that originate from interior evils, which are concupiscences. Illustrated. AE 962:2.
The unchastity lies hidden within like the matter in a wound that is healed only outwardly.
If there is evil in the internal man... the good in the external man is like the superficial healing of a wound, within which there is putrid matter.
On wounds, and filthy tubercles... General article. SE 1762.
Triturated scorpions, mixed with oil (that) absorb all the poison of a wound.
He bound up his wounds, pouring in oil and wine () = to prepare a remedy against the falsities that have injured one's life, by instructing in the good of love and truth of faith. AE 962:6.
Wound () = evil of the will, which is also evil of life.
